# Resux Documentation Index

Resux is an HTML-first public-beta web framework with a custom Vue-like SFC compiler, SSR renderer, serialized resumable state, delegated event runtime, route payload navigation, server APIs, modules, hooks, package modes, first-party media, deployment adapters, optional Vue islands, and a local safety/integrity subsystem.

Framework source: https://github.com/MahmoudAbdalrhmanMohamed/resux
Documentation source: https://github.com/MahmoudAbdalrhmanMohamed/resux-docs
Package: resuxjs
Node requirement in current source: >=20.19.0
Release channels: stable 0.3 via npm latest; public beta 0.4 via npm next
Public-beta milestone: 0.4.0-beta.1

Source code and tests are the documentation source of truth. Do not assume npm latest permanently matches source documentation.

Important facts:
- Resux 0.4 is public beta; APIs may still change before 1.0.
- Use npm `next` for public-beta packages and `latest` for the stable 0.3 line.
- Normal Resux components do not hydrate through Vue.
- `resuxjs/ui` components and `resuxjs/icons` Icon/ResuxIcon are Vue runtime components; use explicit Vue/client contexts.
- `ResuxImg`, `ResuxPicture`, and `ResuxVideo` are handled by the Resux renderer and are not `resuxjs/ui` Vue components.
- The current fonts module is Google-Fonts-only; it does not implement local/self-host font management.
- The current icon module defaults to `collections: []` and `lazy: false`; remote unknown icons load on the client.
- `RxReveal` is mount-triggered, not viewport-triggered; the `vAnime`/`vAnimate` directive is the viewport-observed UI API.
- `RxAutoAnimate` currently runs one mount animation and does not observe child/layout mutations.
- `useFetch` returns an AsyncDataResource with data/value/pending/error refs.
- image transforms require sharp; video transforms require ffmpeg.
- production server/deployment report verification requires RESUX_HALAL_REPORT_SIGNING_SECRET.
